matches.title: San Marino vs Finland
matches.description: Watch San Marino vs Finland highlights and goals from UEFA Nations League on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on September 26, 2026. The UEFA Nations League returned to the spotlight on September 26, 2026, as San Marino played host to Finland in a fixture filled with tactical intrigue. Both sets of supporters gathered with high expectations, witnessing a match that would eventually be defined by clinical finishing and a dramatic shift in momentum. Finland's First-Half Blitz From the opening whistle, Finland established a commanding presence on the pitch. It took only five minutes for Joel Pohjanpalo to find the back of the net, setting a high tempo for the visitors. The pressure didn't stop there; in the 14th minute, Adrian Svanbaeck doubled the lead after being teed up by a clever pass from Leo Walta . San Marino struggled to contain the fluid movement of the Finnish attack, which seemed to find space at will. The dominance continued as the half progressed. In the 33rd minute, Benjamin Kaellman made it three, benefiting from Svanbaeck's vision. While Adam Markhiev picked up a yellow card late in the half, the story of the first 45 minutes was entirely about Finland's efficiency in front of goal and their ability to starve the hosts of possession. Red Card and Defensive Collapse The second half began with immediate fireworks. Leo Walta added his name to the scoresheet in the 50th minute, but the match took a decisive turn just sixty seconds later. San Marino's Alessandro Golinucci was shown a straight red card, sparking heavy protests from his teammates. Reduced to ten men, the uphill battle for the hosts became a mountain that was impossible to climb. With a numerical advantage, Finland struck again almost immediately. Walta secured his second of the night in the 55th minute, assisted by Juho Laehteenmaeki . As the game moved past the hour mark, both managers turned to their benches. San Marino introduced Giacomo Benvenuti and Samuel Pancotti in an attempt to shore up the defense, while Finland brought on the experienced Robin Lod to manage the closing stages. Pohjanpalo Completes the Hat-trick The final ten minutes belonged to Joel Pohjanpalo . In the 79th minute, he netted his second goal of the match following another assist from the industrious Svanbaeck . The misery for San Marino was compounded in the 86th minute when Cristian Meloni conceded a penalty and received a yellow card. Pohjanpalo stepped up to the spot and calmly converted, sealing a brilliant hat-trick in the 87th minute. After six minutes of stoppage time, the referee brought the contest to an end. It was a professional and ruthless display from Finland , who took full advantage of their opportunities and the mid-game dismissal to secure a comprehensive victory on the road.
